chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the testimony of the child of fornication, so he said: 'No, and no slave.'

key_terms.شَهَادَةِ: Testimony or witnesshood in legal contexts
key_terms.وَلَدِ الزِّنَا: Child of fornication (offspring of a zina relationship)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of the testimony of a child born from fornication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the juridical status of a *walad al-zina* (child of fornication) regarding their legal testimony (*shahadah*). The phrase 'la wa la abd' is interpreted by Shia jurists as indicating a unique intermediate rank: their testimony is accepted but carries less weight than that of a free, legitimate Muslim, yet it is superior to that of a slave. This ruling highlights the distinction between lineage legitimacy and legal capacity in Shia fiqh, influencing inheritance and witness validity.
